The caulking exhibited the following defects: Uneven and irregular application -The caulking was applied unevenly along the frame seams, resulting in inconsistent thickness and width, with visible ridges, valleys, and surface irregularities. These surface irregularities cannot be adequately cleaned or disinfected and provide sites where microbial contamination, cleaning solution residue, and particulate matter can accumulate and persist despite cleaning efforts. Rough and porous surface texture -The caulking surface was visibly rough and non-smooth in texture. A porous, rough surface within an ISO 5 critical zone is inherently incompatible with the cleanliness requirements of a sterile environment, as it cannot be effectively wiped down or disinfected and can harbor microbial contamination within its surface irregularities. Discoloration and signs of degradation -The caulking exhibited visible discoloration and signs of aging and chemical degradation, consistent with prolonged exposure to cleaning and disinfecting agents. Degraded caulking material is prone to cracking, flaking, and shedding, generating particles that can directly contaminate the critical production area and the sterile drug products prepared within it. Separation and cracking from the frame surface -The caulking appeared to be pulling away from and separating from the frame surface in areas, creating open crevices that cannot be cleaned or disinfected and that serve as harborage points for microbial contamination and a source of particle generation within the ISO 5 environment.
